citation: Jegadeesh and Titman (1993), Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers
finding: Documents medium-horizon continuation in U.S. equities using winner-minus-loser relative-strength portfolios.

citation: Carhart (1997), On Persistence in Mutual Fund Performance
finding: Adds a one-year momentum factor to mutual fund performance evaluation and links persistence to factor exposures, expenses, and costs.

citation: Hong and Stein (1999), A Unified Theory of Underreaction, Momentum Trading and Overreaction
finding: Provides gradual-information-diffusion theory that can generate underreaction and trend-chasing behavior.

citation: Daniel, Hirshleifer and Subrahmanyam (1998), Investor Psychology and Security Market Under- and Overreactions
finding: Models overconfidence and biased self-attribution as behavioral mechanisms behind under- and overreaction patterns.

citation: Asness, Moskowitz and Pedersen (2013), Value and Momentum Everywhere
finding: Reports value and momentum premia across multiple asset classes and markets, with common factor structure.

citation: Fama and French (2012), Size, Value, and Momentum in International Stock Returns
finding: Reports momentum outside Japan across major regions, with size-related qualifications.
Documents severe episodic losses in momentum, especially around panic/rebound states, and partial forecastability of crashes.
Argues momentum is driven substantially by intermediate-horizon returns rather than the most recent prior returns.

citation: Harvey, Liu and Zhu (2016), ...and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
finding: Argues factor discovery requires higher statistical hurdles due to extensive multiple testing in asset pricing.

citation: McLean and Pontiff (2016), Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?
finding: Finds average out-of-sample and post-publication decay in published return predictors.

citation: Hou, Xue and Zhang (2020), Replicating Anomalies
finding: Finds many published anomalies fail under stricter replication standards, microcap controls, and multiple-testing hurdles.

citation: Chen and Zimmermann (2022), Open Source Cross-Sectional Asset Pricing
finding: Provides open-source replicated signals and test assets for cross-sectional asset pricing research.
